_what: APPEND-ONLY CONTENT DELTA for schema/class-frame-v1.json — envelope, exterior, site and waterfront. No existing class modified.
_why: Two authors. Builder Code owns the structure; the design session owns the five content arrays.
_cutFrom: the 124-class state as merged in PR #66, read from the source.
_howToApply: Append each array to the array of the same name. Nothing to replace this time.
_noStatusBlock: Derived and tested. `contentPassProgress.remaining` needs envelope, exterior and site dropped by hand — three systems land in one delta.
_thisCompletesTheScheduleOverlap: Your PR #66 note: six `house.*` types remained class-less and all six were envelope or site. **All six land here** — `deck`, `garage-door`, `irrigation-backflow`, `outbuilding`, `retaining-wall`, `tree`. The overlap the parse predicted at fifteen component types is now fully realised, and the precedence rule's worked case has every input it needs.
_thirdUnitlessMeasure: `water-chemistry-balance` is deliberately null. pH, free chlorine, alkalinity and hardness are four different scales and the test kit decides which are read — the same reasoning as `register-airflow` and the field app's three unitless moisture items.

_twoRegionalClassesWorthKnowing.waterfront: `dock-floating`, `dock-fixed`, `boat-lift`, `dock-de-icer` and `shoreline-structure` carry a `waterfront` system tag. `seasonal-removal-and-reinstall` was written for a lake intake two systems ago and five waterfront classes needed it — the vocabulary reaching forward rather than being extended.
_twoRegionalClassesWorthKnowing.heatTrace: Older rural stock leans on it hard, and its absence shows up as ice damming rather than as a missing device.

_oneClassThatEarnsItsSplitByDeclaringAnA: `deck-composite` declares `surface-washing` and NOT `deck-sealing`, and carries an opportunity that fires when a household is sealing it anyway. **The split's value is the work it says not to do** — which is the first time in the frame that a class exists mainly to prevent an action.

careCategories.label: Eavestrough and downspout clearing
careCategories.note: The group-buy item — seasonal, universal, and height work, which the owner ruled 2026-08-05 is HouseSteady labour.

careCategories.label: Weatherseal and caulk renewal
careCategories.note: Doors, windows, penetrations. Household-level and the highest-return small task in the envelope.

careCategories.label: Track and roller service
careCategories.note: Sliding patio doors and garage doors. Cleaned and lubricated, not adjusted — spring adjustment is a trade's.

careCategories.label: Hardware lubrication
careCategories.note: Hinges, latches, locks, operators. Cheap, and it is what stops a window being painted shut by neglect.

careCategories.label: Deck sealing or staining
careCategories.note: Wood only. The composite split exists to declare that this does NOT apply.

careCategories.label: Surface washing
careCategories.note: Composite decking, siding, walkways. Cleaned rather than treated.

careCategories.label: Vegetation clearance
careCategories.note: Keeping growth off structures, terminations, beds and walls. The care that is mostly about what you cut back.

careCategories.label: Seasonal blow-out
careCategories.note: Irrigation lines before freezing. A hard date in this climate, not an interval.

careCategories.label: Water chemistry management
careCategories.note: Pools and hot tubs. Frequent, household-level, and the whole of what keeps the equipment alive.

careCategories.label: Filter and basket cleaning
careCategories.note: Pool and hot tub skimmers, pumps and cartridges.

careCategories.label: Culvert and drain clearing
careCategories.note: Silt, leaves and ice from culverts, yard drains and catch basins. Rural essential — the driveway washes out when it is skipped.

inspectionPoints.label: Glazing and seal condition
inspectionPoints.note: Fogging between panes is a failed seal and it is only visible in the right light — worth naming because it is missed.

inspectionPoints.label: Safety reverse and photo-eye function
inspectionPoints.note: Garage door openers. An annual test with a real failure mode behind it, and it is done by obstructing the beam rather than by adjusting anything.

inspectionPoints.label: Spring and cable condition
inspectionPoints.note: Visual only. A torsion spring under load is a trade's and nothing about it is a household task.

inspectionPoints.label: Structure, fasteners and ledger condition
inspectionPoints.note: The ledger connection is where a deck fails catastrophically rather than gradually, and it is the one part nobody looks at.

inspectionPoints.label: Wall face, batter and drainage
inspectionPoints.note: Retaining walls fail from water behind them, not from load in front.

inspectionPoints.label: Downspout discharge distance and direction
inspectionPoints.note: Frequently missing, crushed, or aimed straight at the foundation — which is the commonest avoidable source of basement water.

inspectionPoints.label: Soffit vent clearance at the insulation
inspectionPoints.note: Insulation shifts and blocks them, which is how attic moisture and ice damming start. Access-found: it wants an attic hatch.

inspectionPoints.label: Foundation vent position and operation
inspectionPoints.note: Seasonal open and close. Seized, or left wrong for the season, invites freeze damage one way and pests the other.

inspectionPoints.label: Shoreline face and toe condition
inspectionPoints.note: Wave, ice and water-level exposure. Not a garden retaining wall, which is why v0.2 split it.

inspectionPoints.label: Backflow preventer test record
inspectionPoints.note: Annual testing is a licensed tester's and it produces a certificate. The record is the inspectable thing; the test is not ours.

inspectionPoints.label: Water chemistry balance
inspectionPoints.note: Deliberately unitless. pH, free chlorine, alkalinity and hardness are four different scales and the test kit decides which are read. Third explicit null unit in the frame.

inspectionPoints.label: Barrier, fence and self-latching gate
inspectionPoints.note: Pools and hot tubs. A regulated safety requirement rather than a maintenance item, and the failure is a drowning.

inspectionPoints.label: Lift service record
inspectionPoints.note: Elevators and lifts are inspected under regulation by a licensed contractor. The record is what we hold; the inspection is not ours.

inspectionPoints.label: Catch basin, grate and sump condition

opportunityConditions.label: Downspout discharging at the foundation
opportunityConditions.note: The cheapest fix with the largest consequence in the whole frame.

opportunityConditions.label: Eavestrough under heavy tree cover with no guards
Soffit ventilation blocked at the insulation
Ice-prone eave with no heat trace
opportunityConditions.note: Regional. Older rural stock leans on it hard, and its absence shows up as ice damming rather than as a missing device.

opportunityConditions.label: Tree overhanging a structure or service
Irrigation with no backflow test record
Pool or hot tub without a compliant self-latching barrier
opportunityConditions.note: Regulated, and the failure is a drowning. Named as a specialist referral rather than a task.

opportunityConditions.label: Culvert restricted or silted
opportunityConditions.note: Rural essential — the driveway washes out and the repair is a machine and a day.

opportunityConditions.label: Composite decking being sealed or stained
opportunityConditions.note: Fires when a household is doing work that does nothing and may harm the surface. The class split exists to make this visible.

ownerQuestions.label: Does water collect anywhere after heavy rain?
ownerQuestions.note: Households know their own yard's puddles precisely, and it is the cheapest input to every drainage question.

ownerQuestions.label: Do you get ice damming or icicles along the eaves?
Who opens and closes it for the season?
ownerQuestions.note: Docks, irrigation, foundation vents, pools. Names the coordination partner and reveals whether it happens at all.

ownerQuestions.label: Has anything shifted, settled or moved?
ownerQuestions.note: Walls, decks, shorelines. A household notices a year of movement that a single visit cannot see.

ownerQuestions.label: Is there a service contract on it?
ownerQuestions.note: Pools, hot tubs, lifts and elevators are often already covered, and coordinating against an existing contract beats arranging a second one.

classes.label: Window
classes.note: Operating style is an attribute, not a class. Its count, storey and access are the per-object attributes the frame does not yet carry — the dimension the monthly service design needs for quotable work.

classes.label: Patio door
classes.note: Sliding track and rollers are their own care, which is the whole of the split from a hinged door.

classes.label: Storm door
classes.note: Its closer and its seasonal glass-and-screen change are its own, and neither belongs to the door behind it.

classes.label: Garage door
classes.note: Cleaned and lubricated, never adjusted — a torsion spring under load is a trade's and visual inspection is the whole of our part.

classes.label: Garage door opener
classes.note: A separate object, and the safety-reverse test is annual with a real failure mode behind it. Tested by obstructing the beam, which is operating to learn rather than adjusting.

classes.label: Wood deck
classes.note: The ledger connection is where a deck fails catastrophically rather than gradually, and it is the part nobody looks at.

classes.label: Composite deck
classes.note: Cleaned, never sealed — and declaring that is the useful half. The opportunity fires when a household is doing work that achieves nothing and may harm the surface.

classes.label: Retaining wall
classes.note: Fails from water behind it, not from load in front.

classes.label: Eavestrough
classes.note: The group-buy item — cleaning is seasonal and universal, and it is height work, which the owner ruled is HouseSteady labour.

classes.label: Downspout extension
classes.note: Frequently missing, crushed, or aimed straight at the foundation. The cheapest fix with the largest consequence in the frame. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Soffit vent
classes.note: Insulation shifts and blocks them, which is how attic moisture and ice damming start. No horizon — a vent is part of the soffit.

classes.label: Plumbing vent stack
classes.note: Blocks or leaks at the roof jack, and it is noticed when traps gurgle rather than when it fails. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Exterior vent
classes.note: `ses.termination-reconcile` reconciles against these — every interior fan and duct should arrive at one of them.

classes.label: Heat trace cable
classes.note: Roof and pipe de-icing. Regional — older rural stock leans on it hard, and its absence shows up as ice damming rather than as a missing device. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Foundation vent
classes.note: Seasonal open and close. Seized, or left wrong for the season, invites freeze damage one way and pests the other. No horizon. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Outbuilding
classes.note: Stub component type at v1.11.0 — reported, not an error.

classes.label: Floating dock
classes.note: Seasonal removal, ice heave and anchoring — and `seasonal-removal-and-reinstall` was written for the lake intake before this class needed it.

classes.label: Fixed dock
classes.note: Stays in the water, so structural inspection replaces seasonal removal. That is the whole split.

classes.label: Boat lift
classes.note: Cables, motor and seasonal exposure. Quinte Conservation names it separately from a dock, which is the regional reason it is its own class.

classes.label: Dock de-icer
classes.note: A bubbler is neither dock hardware nor irrigation, and it runs unattended all winter doing the one job nobody checks. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Shoreline protection
classes.note: Seawall, armour stone, riprap. Wave, ice and water-level exposure is not a garden retaining wall.

classes.label: Tree
classes.note: The schedule keys on `tree` with four items; this adds the object-grain half. No replacement horizon — a tree is removed or it is not, and a lifespan band would be a claim nobody can make.

classes.label: Irrigation system
classes.note: Blow-out is a hard seasonal date in this climate rather than an interval — the same shape as `seasonal-drain-down` on a standard hose bib.

classes.label: Backflow preventer
classes.note: Annual testing is a licensed tester's and produces a certificate. The record is the inspectable thing; the test is not ours. Stub type at v1.11.0. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Hot tub
classes.note: A very different object from a pool and the config bundles them — different volume, different chemistry rhythm, and a cover that is a safety device rather than a heat measure.

classes.label: Lift
classes.note: Inspected under regulation by a licensed contractor. The record is what we hold; the inspection is not ours. Stub type at v1.11.0. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Culvert
classes.note: Rural essential. Silts, collapses, freezes — and the driveway washes out, which is a machine and a day rather than a repair.

classes.label: Yard drain or catch basin
classes.note: Spring melt and foundation water.
